Release sampling state in a reused worker

Source: R/worker_cleanup.R
cleanup_worker_state.Rd

Clear package-owned Julia references left by sampling and request garbage collection in both Julia and R. Use this after finishing a simulation task in a persistent worker, before that worker starts another task. For example, mirai daemons and foreach workers can process many models or data sets in one R session; references held by JuliaCall can otherwise keep the previous task's model and data alive after its R function returns.

Usage

cleanup_worker_state()

Value

An invisible logical scalar: TRUE when the initialized bridge was cleaned, FALSE otherwise. Attributes initialized, reason and error distinguish "cleaned", "not_initialized" (a harmless no-op), and "error" (cleanup failed). An uninitialized worker is not initialized as a side effect. Inspect these attributes when diagnosing worker cleanup; cleanup errors are reported in the result rather than replacing an error from the task being cleaned up.

Details

Call this inside the worker, not in the parent R session: it only cleans the process in which it runs. Register it with on.exit(..., add = TRUE) at the start of the worker's task function so cleanup also runs after an error. Finish extracting summaries or saving the fit before cleanup. Remove large local fit objects when they are no longer needed; objects still referenced by your code cannot be collected.

This function does not start or shut down Julia, unload the package or compiled libraries, delete streaming files, or remove saved results. It keeps the worker ready for another task. Allocators can retain freed memory, so a successful cleanup does not guarantee an immediate fall in the process's reported memory use. Cleanup is usually unnecessary when each task's worker exits immediately, or during ordinary interactive sampling where you still want to use the fit.

Persistent worker example. The same task function can be submitted to mirai or foreach. Set the Julia project in each worker when using a nondefault installation, and save a materialized fit before returning a small result to the parent:

run_condition <- function(seed, path, project_dir = NULL) {
  on.exit(PDMPSamplersR::cleanup_worker_state(), add = TRUE)
  PDMPSamplersR::pdmpsamplers_setup(verbose = FALSE,
                                  project_dir = project_dir)
  fit <- PDMPSamplersR::pdmp_sample(
    function(x) x, d = 2, T = 100, seed = seed,
    materialize = TRUE, show_progress = FALSE)
  saveRDS(fit, path)
  rm(fit)
  path
}

# After starting mirai daemons:
job <- mirai::mirai(run_condition(seed, path),
  seed = 1L, path = tempfile(fileext = ".rds"),
  run_condition = run_condition)

# Or, after registering a foreach process-worker backend:
# library(foreach)
# foreach(i = seq_len(10), .export = "run_condition") %dopar% {
#   run_condition(i, sprintf("fit-%03d.rds", i))
# }

Workers must be able to write the supplied paths. Use shared storage if the parent needs to read files produced on another machine. Export or pass run_condition and its inputs according to your scheduler's conventions.
